questions.t: Which storage class is most cost-effective for data that is rarely read but must stay available within milliseconds?
questions.ex: Standard-Infrequent Access suits data that is read less often but still needs millisecond retrieval, at a lower storage price than Standard. Glacier classes need restore time, and instance storage is not durable.

questions.t: Select all actions that help protect sensitive training data.
o: Encrypt data at rest with KMS keys
Make the storage bucket publicly readable
Restrict access with least-privilege IAM roles
Log and audit every data access
questions.ex: Encryption, least-privilege access and audit logging all protect sensitive data. A publicly readable bucket exposes it, so it is never a protective action.

questions.t: Mark each statement as true or false.
s: Accuracy alone is a reliable metric when classes are heavily imbalanced.
A confusion matrix can be built without ground-truth labels.
questions.ex: Accuracy can look high while minority-class performance is poor. L2 regularization penalises large weights. A confusion matrix compares predictions with true labels, so it needs them.

questions.t: A dataset has 12,000 rows. If 20% are held out for testing, how many rows remain for training?
questions.ex: 20% of 12,000 is 2,400 rows held out for testing. 12,000 minus 2,400 leaves 9,600 rows for training.

questions.t: Explain in 100 to 200 words how you would detect and respond to data drift in a production model.
questions.ex: A strong answer compares live input distributions with the training baseline, sets a drift threshold, alerts on breaches, and then retrains or rolls back. It is marked by an examiner.

questions.t: Arrange the machine learning pipeline steps in the correct order, first to last.
questions.ex: Data is collected and validated first. The model is trained on it, evaluated on held-out data, and only then deployed.

questions.t: Which encryption option gives you control over key rotation and access auditing?
questions.ex: Customer-managed keys in AWS KMS let you set rotation policies and audit key use. Default service keys do not give that control.

questions.t: Name the AWS service that manages encryption keys.
questions.ex: AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) creates, stores and rotates the keys used to encrypt data.

questions.passage: A retail analytics team keeps three years of transaction logs in object storage. Most dashboard queries touch only the last 30 days, while a nightly training job reads the full history. Security reviewers require that encryption keys are rotated on schedule and that every key use is logged.
questions.t: Classify each service by its main purpose.
questions.ex: S3 stores objects, EC2 provides compute capacity, and KMS manages encryption keys.

questions.passage: A retail analytics team keeps three years of transaction logs in object storage. Most dashboard queries touch only the last 30 days, while a nightly training job reads the full history. Security reviewers require that encryption keys are rotated on schedule and that every key use is logged.
questions.t: Which change would most reduce cost for the workload described above?
o: Move logs older than 30 days to a colder storage class
Increase the compute size of the nightly job
Disable key rotation to save API calls
Copy all logs to a second bucket
questions.ex: Logs older than 30 days are rarely queried, so a colder storage class cuts storage cost without affecting the dashboards. The other options raise cost or weaken security.

questions.t: I can explain model monitoring to my team without help.
questions.ex: Self-report item. It is not scored.

questions.t: Match each metric to what it measures.
cols: Share of predicted positives that are correct
Share of actual positives that are found
Share of all predictions that are correct
questions.ex: Precision looks at predicted positives, recall at actual positives, and accuracy at all predictions.

questions.t: Amazon S3 offers ____ storage, while Amazon EBS provides ____ block storage for EC2 instances.
questions.ex: S3 is object storage. EBS volumes keep their data independently of the instance, so they are persistent block storage.

questions.passage:
[1] Source data  ->  [2] Feature store  ->  [3] Training job  ->  [4] Endpoint

The four boxes show the parts of a real-time machine learning pipeline, from left to right.
questions.t: Match each numbered box to its role in the pipeline.
questions.ex: Data enters at box 1 to be ingested, is transformed in the feature store, is trained in box 3, and is served from the endpoint.

questions.passage:
Region      Q1     Q3
North      120    180
South      200    210
East        90    160
West       150    170

Values are units sold, in thousands.
questions.t: Which region grew the most between Q1 and Q3?
questions.ex: East grew from 90 to 160, an increase of 70. North grew by 60, West by 20 and South by 10.

questions.t: Three analysts (Ana, Ben and Cho) each sit on a different floor, 1, 2 or 3. Cho is on floor 1. Ben sits on the floor directly above Ana. Match each analyst to a floor.
questions.ex: Cho is on floor 1, which leaves floors 2 and 3 for Ana and Ben. Ben is directly above Ana, so Ana is on floor 2 and Ben on floor 3.

questions.t: Answer yes or no for each statement.
s: Dropout acts as a regularizer during training.
Standardizing features is required before fitting a decision tree.
questions.ex: Dropout randomly disables units during training, which reduces overfitting. Decision trees split on thresholds, so feature scaling is not required.

questions.t: Assertion (A): Accuracy can be misleading on imbalanced data. Reason (R): A model that always predicts the majority class can still score a high accuracy.
o: A and R are true, and R explains A
A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true and R is false
A is false and R is true
questions.ex: Both statements are true, and the reason explains the assertion: predicting only the majority class gives a high accuracy.
